original_criterion.criterion: For a specified shared study resource, bound admitted work; waiting must preserve all folds, repeats, results, and provenance; outputs should agree across parallelism. Measure elapsed time, peak memory, active workers, and waiting. B56 recommends existing max_parallel_folds from the actual study resource and rejects treating 15 per fit / 60 across four fits as measured CPU load or a production workload.
original_criterion.denominator_boundary: B56’s max_parallel_folds language supports a compute/fold reading, but does not expressly include every Runtime CAS or control-store worker. The all-blocking-I/O denominator is not established by the card or current wiring and is a G contract choice.

metric_scope.cpu: R4 active dispatch/physical worker counts are concurrency units, not CPU cores, utilization or CPU-time. BLAS/OpenMP env pins are 1. No CPU utilization/seconds sample is recorded.
metric_scope.memory: Child records resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss; Darwin unit is bytes. One high-water mark per fresh child includes interpreter/pytest, fixtures and both local Runtime+CAS environments through result prep; excludes outer runner/siblings. No explicit memory cap or production memory denominator is established.
metric_scope.active: Configured SharedExecutor.max_workers is a candidate process-wide physical worker limit; current composition shares that owner across MethodBackend dispatch, Runtime CAS, ControlPlaneStore guards and other common-pool uses.
metric_scope.pending: External ThreadPoolExecutor submissions can queue beyond max_workers. The worker/callback saturated nested-submit guard refuses reentrant work, but no total pending cap exists. Test records queue depth and outstanding at each insertion, per-item queue waits, and pending items at diagnostic end; it does not enforce a maximum backlog. End snapshot is not peak history.
metric_scope.timeout: Runtime CAS and ControlPlaneStore guards explicitly use get_shared_executor() with fixed default 1.5s Future.result timeout; the budget covers submit+queue+service. Cancel cannot stop an already-running operation, so late writes can finish after caller timeout. Per-guard *_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS values do not create pools when an executor is explicitly passed.
metric_scope.elapsed: Child captures measured profile elapsed after setup through readback and Runtime teardown plus full child process elapsed including interpreter/pytest. Existing 180s per-child timeout is not newly calibrated from a successful full native run; retain it as current harness bound and record actual walltime.
metric_scope.dispatch_observation_scope: The reported physical_active_workers_peak is incremented around actual MethodDispatcher.dispatch only. Guard operation rows record each operation interval and executor snapshots at call/start/end, but the current test does not derive/assert a single peak of simultaneous shared-pool workers across both method dispatch and blocking-I/O intervals. If G selects aggregate compute+I/O capacity, add that generic interval/high-water check before treating a passing method-only peak as the aggregate property.

engineering_options_before_G_choice.semantics: One process SharedExecutor capacity covers MethodBackend work and blocking Runtime CAS/control-store workers. Keep the 1.5-second end-to-end guard deadline unchanged.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.evidence: Current Runtime CAS and ControlPlaneStore guards explicitly share get_shared_executor(); ordinary external submissions may wait in ThreadPoolExecutor’s pending queue. The existing executor caps physical active workers, but does not bound total pending submissions.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.benefit: One active-worker resource cap and existing owner; no extra pool lifecycle.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.cost_or_gap: A cap-1 caller can wait behind compute or other I/O. The measured two historical CAS calls each exceeded 1.5 seconds including queue+service; exact failed payloads were not retained. A 42KB no-contention write profile saved about 9ms under cProfile and cannot explain the observed 198–216ms caller overrun.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.falsifier: After exact freeze, run all three profiles; if aggregate capacity is chosen, derive one interval-based high-water across actual dispatch and blocking-guard worker intervals, not only the method-dispatch counter. Profile exact concurrent payload metadata without retaining bytes. Reject the optimization as sufficient if both callers still exceed 1.5s or any output/readback is lost.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.queue_choice_required: Specify whether the cap means active workers only or admitted work including pending submissions. If pending is part of the admitted-work bound, add one generic bounded-queue/typed-overload invariant; no current pending cap exists.

engineering_options_before_G_choice.semantics: Read B56 as method/fold compute capacity and give Runtime blocking I/O a separate, explicitly bounded process-scoped capacity shared by all relevant guards. Preserve the 1.5-second submit-through-service deadline.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.evidence: B56 specifically recommends max_parallel_folds from the study resource. An actual guard+FileSystemCAS prototype with a separate one-worker pool completed one delayed write in about 0.89s, but a single worker cannot establish two concurrent ~0.86s writes under 1.5s; two I/O slots are only a minimum experiment for that observed pair, never a default or production recommendation.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.benefit: Separates fold compute admission from blocking persistence and avoids compute occupancy starving CAS/control-store progress.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.cost_or_gap: This is an explicit resource-vector semantic decision. Requires a single process owner across 2+ Runtime instances and all CAS/control-store guards; positive bounded active I/O and pending work; profile conflict handling; context/tenant propagation; cancellation versus late writes; reentrancy; shutdown where closing one Runtime cannot close a sibling owner; and overload behavior.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.falsifier: Run the exact frozen cap-1/cap-2/removal profiles plus multi-Runtime sibling-close, shared-guard, profile-conflict, timeout/late-completion, and bounded-pending probes. Compare complete output/readback equality; do not infer production capacity.

engineering_options_before_G_choice.semantics: Evaluate wiring existing LocalWorkerPool/TaskRouter or a single typed application-scoped MethodComputeAdmission through the current RunLifecycle→run_experiment→MethodBackend route.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.evidence: LocalWorkerPool/TaskRouter exists but does not own the inspected direct Runtime route; no shared typed MethodComputeAdmission was found there.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.benefit: Could place compute admission at the study/workflow owner rather than a generic executor seam.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.cost_or_gap: Requires a wider Runtime-to-Scientist bridge and still leaves blocking-I/O capacity and pending semantics to define; not a stand-alone B56 fix.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.falsifier: Prove every real route and sibling consumer goes through one owner; remove the bridge while preserving declarations and require the competing workload to exceed the configured compute cap.

engineering_options_before_G_choice.semantics: A new scheduler/cluster, one pool per guard or Runtime, raising/splitting the timeout, or staggering producer start.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.disposition: Not justified by current evidence. Per-guard pools multiply capacity; changing the 1.5s deadline changes caller behavior and may mask a resource problem; staggering removes the competing workload being tested. No blanket waiver, clock shift, or deadline green-by-declaration is proposed.
engineering_options_before_G_choice.reconsideration: Only an explicit G contract decision can change deadline semantics; it must name impacted call/status lifecycle and the reason the present deadline is wrong. No such issuer or evidence is present in this packet.

required_questions: Does B56 capacity count only active method/fold compute, or compute plus every Runtime blocking-I/O worker?
Does “admitted work” count only active workers or also queued/pending submissions, and what bounded-overload behavior is required?
If the denominator is compute-only, may one process-scoped bounded Runtime-I/O vector be introduced while preserving the existing 1.5-second total guard deadlines?
minimum_G_decision.locally_best_supported_interpretation: Treat B56 as method/fold compute capacity and make blocking Runtime I/O an explicit bounded process resource vector, keeping the 1.5-second deadline. This is a proposal, not accepted architecture or formal finding closure. It follows B56’s concrete max_parallel_folds route while avoiding silent unbounded I/O, but only G can set the denominator and pending-work semantics.
minimum_G_decision.not_a_claim: The candidate author cannot infer production qualifying workload, capacity budget, or external authority from portable synthetic fixtures, CPU/RSS snapshots, or historical arithmetic.

current_owner_and_reentrancy.compute: MethodBackend uses common_async_tools.run_shared_executor_sync around actual MethodDispatcher dispatch; test removal bypasses that exact seam.
current_owner_and_reentrancy.guards: Runtime CAS and ControlPlaneStore proxies both receive get_shared_executor(); TaskRunner and sync/async bridges can also use this common process pool.
current_owner_and_reentrancy.reentrancy: Worker-thread synchronous call can inline; saturated nested worker/callback submit fails fast; external producer submits queue. Runtime guards cancel queued futures on timeout, but running I/O is cooperative.
current_owner_and_reentrancy.alternate: LocalWorkerPool/TaskRouter exists but is not the owner on this RunLifecycle→run_experiment route. No shared typed MethodComputeAdmission class exists in inspected Runtime/Scientist code.
current_owner_and_reentrancy.minimum_G_choice: Define if B56 shared capacity counts only active method/fold compute or compute plus every Runtime blocking-I/O worker; separately say whether pending submitted work counts as admitted and define its bound. If compute-only, authorize one bounded process I/O vector. Do not change 1.5s.
current_owner_and_reentrancy.lifecycle_boundary: The available prototype is a standalone bounded I/O executor passed to actual BlockingDependencyGuard+FileSystemCAS. It is not yet a process owner shared across all production Runtime CAS/control-store guards; therefore it proves a small mechanism behavior only, not an installed profile or API contract.
